Because the king did not listen to them, all Israel answered him:

“What share do we have in David?

Each man of Israel, go home![a]

public_domain_references.brenton: And she bore him sons; Jeus, and Samoria, and Zaam.

pob.text: After her[a], he took Maacah the daughter of Absalom, and she bore him Abijah, Attai, Ziza, and Shelomith.

spob.text: Afterward, he took Maacah, Absalom’s daughter[a], as his wife. She gave birth to his children: Abijah, Attai, Ziza, and Shelomith.

public_domain_references.bsb: After her, he married Maacah daughter of Absalom, and she bore to him Abijah, Attai, Ziza, and Shelomith.
public_domain_references.web: After her, he took Maacah the granddaughter of Absalom; and she bore him Abijah, Attai, Ziza, and Shelomith.
public_domain_references.asv: And after her he took Maacah the daughter of Absalom; and she bare him Abijah, and Attai, and Ziza, and Shelomith.

public_domain_references.brenton: And afterwards he took to himself Maacha the daughter of Abessalom; and she bore him Abia, and Jetthi, and Zeza, and Salemoth.

pob.text: Rehoboam loved Maacah the daughter of Absalom more than all his wives and his concubines[a], for he had taken eighteen wives and sixty concubines, and he fathered twenty-eight sons and sixty daughters.

spob.text: Rehoboam loved Maacah, the daughter of Absalom,[a] more than all his other wives and concubines.[b] His household included eighteen wives and sixty concubines in all. He fathered twenty-eight sons and sixty daughters.

public_domain_references.bsb: Rehoboam loved Maacah daughter of Absalom more than all his wives and concubines. In all, he had eighteen wives and sixty concubines, and he was the father of twenty-eight sons and sixty daughters.
public_domain_references.web: Rehoboam loved Maacah the granddaughter of Absalom above all his wives and his concubines; for he took eighteen wives and sixty concubines, and became the father of twenty-eight sons and sixty daughters.
public_domain_references.asv: And Rehoboam loved Maacah the daughter of Absalom above all his wives and his concubines (for he took eighteen wives, and threescore concubines, and begat twenty and eight sons and threescore daughters).
public_domain_references.kjv: And Rehoboam loved Maachah the daughter of Absalom above all his wives and his concubines: (for he took eighteen wives, and threescore concubines; and begat twenty and eight sons, and threescore daughters.)
public_domain_references.brenton: And Roboam loved Maacha the daughter of Abessalom more than all his wives and all his concubines: for he had eighteen wives and sixty concubines; and he begot twenty-eight sons, and sixty daughters.

pob.text: And Rehoboam appointed Abijah son of Maacah as chief among his brothers[a], for he intended to make him king.

spob.text: Rehoboam appointed Abijah son of Maacah as the chief leader among his brothers.[a] He did this because he intended to make Abijah king.

public_domain_references.bsb: Rehoboam appointed Abijah son of Maacah as chief prince among his brothers, intending to make him king.
public_domain_references.web: Rehoboam appointed Abijah the son of Maacah to be chief, the prince among his brothers, for he intended to make him king.
public_domain_references.asv: And Rehoboam appointed Abijah the son of Maacah to be chief, [even] the prince among his brethren; for [he was minded] to make him king.
public_domain_references.kjv: And Rehoboam made Abijah the son of Maachah the chief, [to be] ruler among his brethren: for [he thought] to make him king.
public_domain_references.brenton: And he made Abia the son of Maacha chief, [even] a leader among his brethren, for he intended to make him king.

pob.text: And he acted wisely and distributed some of all his sons throughout all the lands of Judah and Benjamin[a], to all the fortified cities[c][b]; and he gave them abundant provisions and sought many wives for them.

spob.text: He acted wisely by stationing some of his sons throughout the regions of Judah and Benjamin, among all the fortified cities. He gave them plenty of food and arranged for them to have many wives.

public_domain_references.bsb: Rehoboam also acted wisely by dispersing some of his sons throughout the districts of Judah and Benjamin, and to all the fortified cities. He gave them abundant provisions and sought many wives for them.
public_domain_references.web: He dealt wisely, and dispersed some of his sons throughout all the lands of Judah and Benjamin, to every fortified city. He gave them food in abundance; and he sought many wives for them.
public_domain_references.asv: And he dealt wisely, and dispersed of all his sons throughout all the lands of Judah and Benjamin, unto every fortified city: and he gave them victuals in abundance. And he sought [for them] many wives.
public_domain_references.kjv: And he dealt wisely, and dispersed of all his children throughout all the countries of Judah and Benjamin, unto every fenced city: and he gave them victual in abundance. And he desired many wives.
public_domain_references.brenton: And he was exalted beyond all his [other] sons in all the coasts of Juda and Benjamin, and in the strong cities; and he gave them provisions in great abundance: and he desired many wives.

pob.text: And when Rehoboam’s kingdom was established[a], and he had become strong, he abandoned the law of Yahweh—and all Israel with him.

spob.text: Once Rehoboam’s kingdom was firmly established and he was secure in power, he abandoned Yahweh’s law.[a] All Israel joined him in abandoning it.

public_domain_references.bsb: After Rehoboam had established his sovereignty and royal power, he and all Israel with him forsook the Law of the LORD.
public_domain_references.web: When the kingdom of Rehoboam was established and he was strong, he abandoned Yahweh’s law, and all Israel with him.
public_domain_references.asv: And it came to pass, when the kingdom of Rehoboam was established, and he was strong, that he forsook the law of Jehovah, and all Israel with him.
public_domain_references.kjv: And it came to pass, when Rehoboam had established the kingdom, and had strengthened himself, he forsook the law of the LORD, and all Israel with him.
public_domain_references.brenton: And it came to pass when the kingdom of Roboam was established, and when he had grown strong, [that] he forsook the commandments of the Lord, and all Israel with him.

pob.text: And in the fifth year of King Rehoboam[a], Shishak king of Egypt came up against Jerusalem, because they had acted unfaithfully against Yahweh.

spob.text: In the fifth year of King Rehoboam’s reign, King Shishak of Egypt marched against Jerusalem because the people had broken faith with the LORD.

public_domain_references.bsb: In the fifth year of Rehoboam’s reign, because they had been unfaithful to the LORD, Shishak king of Egypt came up and attacked Jerusalem
public_domain_references.web: In the fifth year of King Rehoboam, Shishak king of Egypt came up against Jerusalem, because they had trespassed against Yahweh,
public_domain_references.asv: And it came to pass in the fifth year of king Rehoboam, that Shishak king of Egypt came up against Jerusalem, because they had trespassed against Jehovah,
public_domain_references.kjv: And it came to pass, [that] in the fifth year of king Rehoboam Shishak king of Egypt came up against Jerusalem, because they had transgressed against the LORD,
public_domain_references.brenton: And it came to pass in the fifth year of the reign of Roboam, Susakim king of Egypt came up against Jerusalem, because they had sinned against the Lord,

pob.text: with 1,200 chariots and 60,000 horsemen[a], and the people who came with him from Egypt were without number: Libyans, Sukkites[c][b], and Cushites.

spob.text: He came with 1,200 chariots and 60,000 horsemen. Countless people also came with him from Egypt: Libyans, Sukkites[a], and Cushites.[b]

public_domain_references.bsb: with 1,200 chariots, 60,000 horsemen, and countless troops who came with him out of Egypt—Libyans, Sukkites, and Cushites.
public_domain_references.web: with twelve hundred chariots and sixty thousand horsemen. The people were without number who came with him out of Egypt: the Lubim, the Sukkiim, and the Ethiopians.
public_domain_references.asv: with twelve hundred chariots, and threescore thousand horsemen. And the people were without number that came with him out of Egypt: the Lubim, the Sukkiim, and the Ethiopians.
public_domain_references.kjv: With twelve hundred chariots, and threescore thousand horsemen: and the people [were] without number that came with him out of Egypt; the Lubims, the Sukkiims, and the Ethiopians.
public_domain_references.brenton: with twelve hundred chariots, and sixty thousand horse: and there was no number of the multitude that came with him from Egypt; Libyans, Trogodytes, and Ethiopians.

pob.text: He captured the fortified cities that belonged to Judah and came as far as Jerusalem[a].

spob.text: He captured Judah’s fortified cities. Then he came as far as Jerusalem.[a]

public_domain_references.bsb: He captured the fortified cities of Judah and came as far as Jerusalem.
public_domain_references.web: He took the fortified cities which belonged to Judah, and came to Jerusalem.
public_domain_references.asv: And he took the fortified cities which pertained to Judah, and came unto Jerusalem.
public_domain_references.kjv: And he took the fenced cities which [pertained] to Judah, and came to Jerusalem.
public_domain_references.brenton: And they obtained possession of the strong cities, which were in Juda, and came to Jerusalem.

pob.text: Then Shemaiah the prophet came to Rehoboam and the officials of Judah who had gathered in Jerusalem because of Shishak[a], and he said to them, “Thus says Yahweh: You have forsaken me, so I also have forsaken you into the hand of Shishak.”

spob.text: Then the prophet Shemaiah came to Rehoboam and the officials of Judah. They had gathered in Jerusalem because Shishak was advancing against them. Shemaiah said, “This is what Yahweh says: ‘You abandoned me, so I have also abandoned you, giving you over to Shishak’s power.’”

public_domain_references.bsb: Then Shemaiah the prophet came to Rehoboam and the leaders of Judah who had gathered at Jerusalem because of Shishak, and he said to them, “This is what the LORD says: ‘You have forsaken Me; therefore, I have forsaken you into the hand of Shishak.’”
public_domain_references.web: Now Shemaiah the prophet came to Rehoboam and to the princes of Judah, who were gathered together to Jerusalem because of Shishak, and said to them, “Yahweh says, ‘You have forsaken me, therefore I have also left you in the hand of Shishak.’”
public_domain_references.asv: Now Shemaiah the prophet came to Rehoboam, and to the princes of Judah, that were gathered together to Jerusalem because of Shishak, and said unto them, Thus saith Jehovah, Ye have forsaken me, therefore have I also left you in the hand of Shishak.
public_domain_references.kjv: ¶ Then came Shemaiah the prophet to Rehoboam, and [to] the princes of Judah, that were gathered together to Jerusalem because of Shishak, and said unto them, Thus saith the LORD, Ye have forsaken me, and therefore have I also left you in the hand of Shishak.
public_domain_references.brenton: And Samaias the prophet came to Roboam, and to the princes of Juda that were gathered to Jerusalem for fear of Susakim, and said to them, Thus said the Lord, Ye have left me, and I will leave you in the hand of Susakim.

pob.text: Then the leaders of Israel and the king humbled themselves and said[a], “Yahweh is righteous.”

spob.text: Then Israel’s leaders[a] and the king humbled themselves. They said, “Yahweh is righteous.”

public_domain_references.bsb: So the leaders of Israel and the king humbled themselves and said, “The LORD is righteous.”
public_domain_references.web: Then the princes of Israel and the king humbled themselves; and they said, “Yahweh is righteous.”
public_domain_references.asv: Then the princes of Israel and the king humbled themselves; and they said, Jehovah is righteous.
public_domain_references.kjv: Whereupon the princes of Israel and the king humbled themselves; and they said, The LORD [is] righteous.
public_domain_references.brenton: And the elders of Israel and the king were ashamed, and said, The Lord [is] righteous.

pob.text: When Yahweh saw that they had humbled themselves[a], the word of Yahweh came to Shemaiah, saying, “They have humbled themselves; I will not destroy them, but I will grant them some deliverance, and my wrath will not be poured out on Jerusalem by the hand of Shishak.”

spob.text: When Yahweh saw that they had humbled themselves, Yahweh’s word came to Shemaiah: “They have humbled themselves. I will not destroy them. I will rescue them, but only to a limited extent.[a] I will not pour out my wrath on Jerusalem through Shishak.”

public_domain_references.bsb: When the LORD saw that they had humbled themselves, the word of the LORD came to Shemaiah, saying, “They have humbled themselves; I will not destroy them, but will soon grant them deliverance. My wrath will not be poured out on Jerusalem through Shishak.
public_domain_references.web: When Yahweh saw that they humbled themselves, Yahweh’s word came to Shemaiah, saying, “They have humbled themselves. I will not destroy them, but I will grant them some deliverance, and my wrath won’t be poured out on Jerusalem by the hand of Shishak.
public_domain_references.asv: And when Jehovah saw that they humbled themselves, the word of Jehovah came to Shemaiah, saying, They have humbled themselves: I will not destroy them; but I will grant them some deliverance, and my wrath shall not be poured out upon Jerusalem by the hand of Shishak.
public_domain_references.kjv: And when the LORD saw that they humbled themselves, the word of the LORD came to Shemaiah, saying, They have humbled themselves; [therefore] I will not destroy them, but I will grant them some deliverance; and my wrath shall not be poured out upon Jerusalem by the hand of Shishak.
public_domain_references.brenton: And when the Lord saw that they repented, then came the word of the Lord to Samaias, saying, They have repented; I will not destroy them, but I will set them in safety for a little while, and my wrath shall not be poured out on Jerusalem.

pob.text: For they will become his slaves[a], so that they may know my service and the service of the kingdoms of the lands.

spob.text: For they will become his slaves. In this way, they will learn what it means to serve me[a] and what it means to serve the kingdoms of other lands.

public_domain_references.bsb: Nevertheless, they will become his servants, so that they may learn the difference between serving Me and serving the kings of other lands.”
public_domain_references.web: Nevertheless they will be his servants, that they may know my service, and the service of the kingdoms of the countries.”
public_domain_references.asv: Nevertheless they shall be his servants, that they may know my service, and the service of the kingdoms of the countries.
public_domain_references.kjv: Nevertheless they shall be his servants; that they may know my service, and the service of the kingdoms of the countries.
public_domain_references.brenton: Nevertheless they shall be servants, and know my service, and the service of the kings of the earth.

pob.text: So Shishak king of Egypt came up against Jerusalem and took the treasuries of the house of Yahweh and the treasuries of the king’s house[a]. He took everything[b]; he also took the gold shields that Solomon had made.

spob.text: So Shishak king of Egypt attacked Jerusalem. He took the treasures from Yahweh’s temple and from the royal palace. He took everything. He even took the gold shields Solomon had made.

public_domain_references.bsb: So King Shishak of Egypt attacked Jerusalem and seized the treasures of the house of the LORD and of the royal palace. He took everything, including the gold shields that Solomon had made.
public_domain_references.web: So Shishak king of Egypt came up against Jerusalem and took away the treasures of Yahweh’s house and the treasures of the king’s house. He took it all away. He also took away the shields of gold which Solomon had made.
public_domain_references.asv: So Shishak king of Egypt came up against Jerusalem, and took away the treasures of the house of Jehovah, and the treasures of the king’s house: he took all away: he took away also the shields of gold which Solomon had made.
public_domain_references.kjv: So Shishak king of Egypt came up against Jerusalem, and took away the treasures of the house of the LORD, and the treasures of the king’s house; he took all: he carried away also the shields of gold which Solomon had made.
public_domain_references.brenton: So Susakim king of Egypt went up against Jerusalem, and took the treasures that were in the house of the Lord, and the treasures that were in the king's house: he took all; and he took the golden shields which Solomon had made.

pob.text: So King Rehoboam made bronze shields in their place and committed them to the care of the commanders of the guards[b][a], who kept watch at the entrance of the king’s house.

spob.text: So King Rehoboam made bronze shields to replace the gold shields that had been taken. He entrusted them to the commanders of the palace guards,[a] who kept watch at the entrance to the king’s palace.

public_domain_references.bsb: Then King Rehoboam made bronze shields in their place and committed them to the care of the captains of the guard on duty at the entrance to the royal palace.
public_domain_references.web: King Rehoboam made shields of bronze in their place, and committed them to the hands of the captains of the guard, who kept the door of the king’s house.
public_domain_references.asv: And king Rehoboam made in their stead shields of brass, and committed them to the hands of the captains of the guard, that kept the door of the king’s house.
public_domain_references.kjv: Instead of which king Rehoboam made shields of brass, and committed [them] to the hands of the chief of the guard, that kept the entrance of the king’s house.
public_domain_references.brenton: And king Roboam made brazen shields instead of them. And Susakim set over him captains of footmen, as keepers of the gate of the king.

pob.text: And whenever the king entered the house of Yahweh[a], the guards would come and carry them[c][b], and then return them to the guards’ chamber.

spob.text: Whenever the king entered Yahweh’s temple, the guards came and carried the bronze shields. Then they returned the shields to the guardroom.

public_domain_references.bsb: And whenever the king entered the house of the LORD, the guards would go with him, bearing the shields, and later they would return them to the guardroom.
public_domain_references.web: As often as the king entered into Yahweh’s house, the guard came and bore them, then brought them back into the guard room.
public_domain_references.asv: And it was so, that, as oft as the king entered into the house of Jehovah, the guard came and bare them, and brought them back into the guard-chamber.
public_domain_references.kjv: And when the king entered into the house of the LORD, the guard came and fetched them, and brought them again into the guard chamber.
public_domain_references.brenton: And it came to pass, when the king went into the house of the Lord, the guards and the footmen went in, and they that returned to meet the footmen.

pob.text: And when he humbled himself[a], the anger of Yahweh turned away from him, so as not to destroy him completely[b]; and also in Judah there were good things.

spob.text: When Rehoboam humbled himself, Yahweh turned his anger away from him and did not destroy him completely. There were also good things in Judah.[a]

public_domain_references.bsb: Because Rehoboam humbled himself, the anger of the LORD turned away from him, and He did not destroy him completely. Indeed, conditions were good in Judah.
public_domain_references.web: When he humbled himself, Yahweh’s wrath turned from him, so as not to destroy him altogether. Moreover, there were good things found in Judah.
public_domain_references.asv: And when he humbled himself, the wrath of Jehovah turned from him, so as not to destroy him altogether: and moreover in Judah there were good things [found].
public_domain_references.kjv: And when he humbled himself, the wrath of the LORD turned from him, that he would not destroy [him] altogether: and also in Judah things went well.
public_domain_references.brenton: And when he repented, the anger of the Lord turned from him, and did not destroy him utterly; for there were good things in Juda.

pob.text: So King Rehoboam strengthened himself in Jerusalem and reigned[a]. Rehoboam was forty-one years old when he began to reign, and he reigned seventeen years in Jerusalem, the city that Yahweh had chosen from all the tribes of Israel to put his name there[b]. And his mother’s name was Naamah the Ammonite.

spob.text: King Rehoboam strengthened his rule in Jerusalem and reigned. He was forty-one years old when he began to reign, and he ruled in Jerusalem for seventeen years. Yahweh had chosen Jerusalem from among all the tribes of Israel as the city where he would put his name. Rehoboam’s mother was Naamah, an Ammonite.[a]

public_domain_references.bsb: Thus King Rehoboam established himself in Jerusalem. He was forty-one years old when he became king, and he reigned seventeen years in Jerusalem, the city the LORD had chosen from all the tribes of Israel in which to put His Name. His mother’s name was Naamah the Ammonite.
public_domain_references.web: So King Rehoboam strengthened himself in Jerusalem and reigned; for Rehoboam was forty-one years old when he began to reign, and he reigned seventeen years in Jerusalem, the city which Yahweh had chosen out of all the tribes of Israel to put his name there. His mother’s name was Naamah the Ammonitess.
public_domain_references.asv: So king Rehoboam strengthened himself in Jerusalem, and reigned: for Rehoboam was forty and one years old when he began to reign, and he reigned seventeen years in Jerusalem, the city which Jehovah had chosen out of all the tribes of Israel, to put his name there: and his mother’s name was Naamah the Ammonitess.
public_domain_references.kjv: ¶ So king Rehoboam strengthened himself in Jerusalem, and reigned: for Rehoboam [was] one and forty years old when he began to reign, and he reigned seventeen years in Jerusalem, the city which the LORD had chosen out of all the tribes of Israel, to put his name there. And his mother’s name [was] Naamah an Ammonitess.
public_domain_references.brenton: So king Roboam strengthened [himself] in Jerusalem, and reigned: and Roboam was forty and one years old when he began to reign, and he reigned seventeen years in Jerusalem, in the city which the Lord chose out of all the tribes of the children of Israel to call his name there: and his mother's name was Noomma the Ammanitess.

pob.text: And he did what was evil[a], because he had not set his heart to seek Yahweh.

spob.text: He did what was evil because he had not resolved in his heart to seek Yahweh.

public_domain_references.bsb: And Rehoboam did evil because he did not set his heart to seek the LORD.
public_domain_references.web: He did that which was evil, because he didn’t set his heart to seek Yahweh.
public_domain_references.asv: And he did that which was evil, because he set not his heart to seek Jehovah.
public_domain_references.kjv: And he did evil, because he prepared not his heart to seek the LORD.
public_domain_references.brenton: And he did evil, for he directed not his heart to seek the Lord.

pob.text: The acts of Rehoboam[a], the first and the last, are they not written in the records of Shemaiah the prophet and of Iddo the seer, according to genealogical enrollment? And there were wars between Rehoboam and Jeroboam all their days.

spob.text: Everything Rehoboam did as king, from beginning to end—is it not recorded in the writings of Shemaiah the prophet and Iddo the seer, in genealogical records?[a] There was war between Rehoboam and Jeroboam all their days.

public_domain_references.bsb: Now the acts of Rehoboam, from first to last, are they not written in the records of Shemaiah the Prophet and of Iddo the Seer concerning the genealogies? There was war between Rehoboam and Jeroboam throughout their days.
public_domain_references.web: Now the acts of Rehoboam, first and last, aren’t they written in the histories of Shemaiah the prophet and of Iddo the seer, in the genealogies? There were wars between Rehoboam and Jeroboam continually.
public_domain_references.asv: Now the acts of Rehoboam, first and last, are they not written in the histories of Shemaiah the prophet and of Iddo the seer, after the manner of genealogies? And there were wars between Rehoboam and Jeroboam continually.
public_domain_references.kjv: Now the acts of Rehoboam, first and last, [are] they not written in the book of Shemaiah the prophet, and of Iddo the seer concerning genealogies? And [there were] wars between Rehoboam and Jeroboam continually.
public_domain_references.brenton: And the acts of Roboam, the first and the last, behold, are they not written in the book of Samaia the prophet, and Addo the seer, with his achievements.

pob.text: And Rehoboam slept with his fathers and was buried in the city of David[a], and Abijah his son reigned in his place.

spob.text: Rehoboam slept with his ancestors in death[a] and was buried in the City of David. His son Abijah became king in his place.

public_domain_references.bsb: And Rehoboam rested with his fathers and was buried in the City of David. And his son Abijah reigned in his place.
public_domain_references.web: Rehoboam slept with his fathers, and was buried in David’s city; and Abijah his son reigned in his place.
public_domain_references.asv: And Rehoboam slept with his fathers, and was buried in the city of David: and Abijah his son reigned in his stead.
public_domain_references.kjv: And Rehoboam slept with his fathers, and was buried in the city of David: and Abijah his son reigned in his stead.
public_domain_references.brenton: And Roboam made war with Jeroboam all [his] days. And Roboam died with his fathers, and was buried in the city of David: and Abia his son reigned in his stead.

pob.text: In the eighteenth year of King Jeroboam[a], Abijah became king over Judah.

spob.text: During King Jeroboam’s eighteenth year as king, Abijah[a] became king of Judah.

public_domain_references.bsb: In the eighteenth year of Jeroboam’s reign, Abijah became king of Judah,
public_domain_references.web: In the eighteenth year of King Jeroboam, Abijah began to reign over Judah.
public_domain_references.asv: In the eighteenth year of king Jeroboam began Abijah to reign over Judah.
public_domain_references.kjv: Now in the eighteenth year of king Jeroboam began Abijah to reign over Judah.
public_domain_references.brenton: In the eighteenth year of the reign of Jeroboam Abia began to reign over Juda.

pob.text: He reigned three years in Jerusalem[a], and his mother’s name was Micaiah daughter of Uriel from Gibeah. And there was war between Abijah and Jeroboam.

spob.text: He was king in Jerusalem for three years. His mother was Micaiah,[a] daughter of Uriel from Gibeah. Abijah and Jeroboam were at war with each other.

public_domain_references.bsb: and he reigned in Jerusalem three years. His mother’s name was Micaiah daughter of Uriel; she was from Gibeah. And there was war between Abijah and Jeroboam.
public_domain_references.web: He reigned three years in Jerusalem. His mother’s name was Micaiah the daughter of Uriel of Gibeah. There was war between Abijah and Jeroboam.
public_domain_references.asv: Three years reigned he in Jerusalem: and his mother’s name was Micaiah the daughter of Uriel of Gibeah. And there was war between Abijah and Jeroboam.
public_domain_references.kjv: He reigned three years in Jerusalem. His mother’s name also [was] Michaiah the daughter of Uriel of Gibeah. And there was war between Abijah and Jeroboam.
public_domain_references.brenton: He reigned three years in Jerusalem. And his mother's name [was] Maacha, daughter of Uriel of Gabaon. And there was war between Abia and Jeroboam.

pob.text: Abijah joined battle with an army of four hundred thousand chosen men[a], mighty warriors; and Jeroboam drew up for battle against him with eight hundred thousand chosen men[b], mighty men of valor.

spob.text: Abijah went into battle with an army of 400,000 chosen, mighty warriors. Jeroboam formed his troops for battle against him with 800,000 chosen, valiant warriors.

public_domain_references.bsb: Abijah went into battle with an army of 400,000 chosen men, while Jeroboam drew up in formation against him with 800,000 chosen and mighty men of valor.
public_domain_references.web: Abijah joined battle with an army of valiant men of war, even four hundred thousand chosen men; and Jeroboam set the battle in array against him with eight hundred thousand chosen men, who were mighty men of valor.
public_domain_references.asv: And Abijah joined battle with an army of valiant men of war, even four hundred thousand chosen men: and Jeroboam set the battle in array against him with eight hundred thousand chosen men, who were mighty men of valor.
public_domain_references.kjv: And Abijah set the battle in array with an army of valiant men of war, [even] four hundred thousand chosen men: Jeroboam also set the battle in array against him with eight hundred thousand chosen men, [being] mighty men of valour.
public_domain_references.brenton: And Abia set the battle in array with an army, with mighty men of war, [even] four hundred thousand mighty men: and Jeroboam set the battle in array against him with eight hundred thousand, [they were] mighty warriors of the host.

pob.text: Then Abijah stood on Mount Zemaraim[a], which is in the hill country of Ephraim, and said, “Hear me, Jeroboam and all Israel!”

public_domain_references.brenton: And Abia rose up from the mount Somoron, which is in mount Ephraim, and said, Hear ye, Jeroboam, and all Israel:

pob.text: Do you not know that Yahweh[a], the God of Israel, gave the kingdom over Israel to David forever, to him and to his sons[b], by a covenant of salt?

spob.text: Do you not know that Yahweh, the God of Israel, gave David and his sons[a] the right to rule Israel forever? He established this by a covenant of salt.[b]

public_domain_references.bsb: Do you not know that the LORD, the God of Israel, has given the kingship of Israel to David and his descendants forever by a covenant of salt ?
public_domain_references.web: Ought you not to know that Yahweh, the God of Israel, gave the kingdom over Israel to David forever, even to him and to his sons by a covenant of salt?

public_domain_references.kjv: Ought ye not to know that the LORD God of Israel gave the kingdom over Israel to David for ever, [even] to him and to his sons by a covenant of salt?
public_domain_references.brenton: [Is it] not for you to know that the Lord God of Israel has given a king over Israel for ever to David, and to his sons, by a covenant of salt?

pob.text: Jeroboam son of Nebat[a], a servant of Solomon son of David, rose up and rebelled against his lord.

spob.text: Jeroboam son of Nebat was a servant of Solomon son of David. He rose up and rebelled against his lord.[a]

public_domain_references.bsb: Yet Jeroboam son of Nebat, a servant of Solomon son of David, rose up and rebelled against his master.
public_domain_references.web: Yet Jeroboam the son of Nebat, the servant of Solomon the son of David, rose up, and rebelled against his lord.

public_domain_references.kjv: Yet Jeroboam the son of Nebat, the servant of Solomon the son of David, is risen up, and hath rebelled against his lord.
public_domain_references.brenton: But Jeroboam the [son] of Nabat, the servant of Solomon [the son] of David, is risen up, and has revolted from his master:

pob.text: And worthless men[a], sons of Belial, gathered around him and proved stronger than Rehoboam son of Solomon, when Rehoboam was young and fainthearted and had not strengthened himself against them.

spob.text: Worthless men—sons of Belial[a]—gathered around him and proved stronger than Rehoboam son of Solomon. At that time, Rehoboam was young, lacked courage, and had not made himself strong enough to resist them.

public_domain_references.bsb: Then worthless and wicked men gathered around him to resist Rehoboam son of Solomon when he was young, inexperienced, and unable to resist them.
public_domain_references.web: Worthless men were gathered to him, wicked fellows who strengthened themselves against Rehoboam the son of Solomon, when Rehoboam was young and tender hearted, and could not withstand them.
public_domain_references.asv: And there were gathered unto him worthless men, base fellows, that strengthened themselves against Rehoboam the son of Solomon, when Rehoboam was young and tender-hearted, and could not withstand them.
public_domain_references.kjv: And there are gathered unto him vain men, the children of Belial, and have strengthened themselves against Rehoboam the son of Solomon, when Rehoboam was young and tenderhearted, and could not withstand them.
public_domain_references.brenton: and there are gathered to him pestilent men, transgressors, and he has risen up against Roboam the [son] of Solomon, while Roboam was young and fearful in heart, and he withstood him not.

pob.text: And now you are saying that you are strong enough to stand against the kingdom of Yahweh in the hand of the sons of David[c][b][a], because you are a great multitude and have with you the golden calves that Jeroboam made for you as gods.

spob.text: Now you claim that you are strong enough to stand against the kingdom of Yahweh, ruled through David’s descendants. You make this claim because there are so many of you and because you have the golden calves that Jeroboam made for you as gods.

public_domain_references.bsb: And now you think you can resist the kingdom of the LORD, which is in the hands of David’s descendants. You are indeed a vast army, and you have with you the golden calves that Jeroboam made for you as gods.
public_domain_references.web: “Now you intend to withstand the kingdom of Yahweh in the hand of the sons of David. You are a great multitude, and the golden calves which Jeroboam made you for gods are with you.
public_domain_references.asv: And now ye think to withstand the kingdom of Jehovah in the hand of the sons of David; and ye are a great multitude, and there are with you the golden calves which Jeroboam made you for gods.
public_domain_references.kjv: And now ye think to withstand the kingdom of the LORD in the hand of the sons of David; and ye [be] a great multitude, and [there are] with you golden calves, which Jeroboam made you for gods.
public_domain_references.brenton: And now ye profess to resist the kingdom of the Lord in the hand of the sons of David; and ye [are] a great multitude, and with you are golden calves, which Jeroboam made you for gods.

pob.text: Have you not driven out the priests of Yahweh[a], the sons of Aaron and the Levites[b], and made priests for yourselves like the peoples of the lands? Whoever comes to fill his hand with a young bull and seven rams becomes a priest of what are not gods.

spob.text: Did you not drive out Yahweh’s priests—the sons of Aaron—and the Levites, and then appoint your own priests as the peoples of other lands do? Anyone who brings a young bull and seven rams to be ordained[a] becomes a priest of what are not gods.[b]

public_domain_references.bsb: But did you not drive out the priests of the LORD, the sons of Aaron, and the Levites? And did you not make priests for yourselves as do the peoples of other lands? Now whoever comes to consecrate himself with a young bull and seven rams can become a priest of things that are not gods.
public_domain_references.web: Haven’t you driven out the priests of Yahweh, the sons of Aaron, and the Levites, and made priests for yourselves according to the ways of the peoples of other lands? Whoever comes to consecrate himself with a young bull and seven rams may be a priest of those who are no gods.
public_domain_references.asv: Have ye not driven out the priests of Jehovah, the sons of Aaron, and the Levites, and made you priests after the manner of the peoples of [other] lands? so that whosoever cometh to consecrate himself with a young bullock and seven rams, the same may be a priest of [them that are] no gods.
public_domain_references.kjv: Have ye not cast out the priests of the LORD, the sons of Aaron, and the Levites, and have made you priests after the manner of the nations of [other] lands? so that whosoever cometh to consecrate himself with a young bullock and seven rams, [the same] may be a priest of [them that are] no gods.
public_domain_references.brenton: Did ye not cast out the priests of the Lord, the sons of Aaron, and the Levites, and make to yourselves priests of the people of any [other] land? whoever came to consecrate himself with a calf of the herd and seven rams, he forthwith became a priest to that which is no god.

pob.text: But as for us[a], Yahweh is our God, and we have not forsaken him; and the priests who minister to Yahweh are the sons of Aaron[b], and the Levites are in their work.

spob.text: But as for us, Yahweh is our God, and we have not abandoned him. The priests who serve Yahweh are Aaron’s descendants, and the Levites carry out their assigned work.

public_domain_references.bsb: But as for us, the LORD is our God. We have not forsaken Him; the priests who minister to the LORD are sons of Aaron, and the Levites attend to their duties.
public_domain_references.web: “But as for us, Yahweh is our God, and we have not forsaken him. We have priests serving Yahweh, the sons of Aaron, and the Levites in their work.

pob.text: And we offer up burnt offerings to Yahweh morning by morning and evening by evening[a], and fragrant incense, and the arrangement of bread on the pure table, and the golden lampstand with its lamps to burn evening by evening; for we are keeping the charge of Yahweh our God, but you have forsaken him.

spob.text: Every morning and every evening, we offer burnt offerings to Yahweh and burn fragrant incense. We arrange the bread[a] on the ceremonially pure table, and every evening we light the lamps of the golden lampstand. We carry out the duties Yahweh our God has given us, but you have abandoned him.

public_domain_references.bsb: Every morning and every evening they present burnt offerings and fragrant incense to the LORD. They set out the rows of showbread on the ceremonially clean table, and every evening they light the lamps of the gold lampstand. public_domain_references.web: They burn to Yahweh every morning and every evening burnt offerings and sweet incense. public_domain_references.kjv: And they burn unto the LORD every morning and every evening burnt sacrifices and sweet incense: the shewbread also [set they in order] upon the pure table; and the candlestick of gold with the lamps thereof, to burn every evening: for we keep the charge of the LORD our God; but ye have forsaken him.
public_domain_references.brenton: they sacrifice to the Lord whole-burnt-offering, morning and evening, and compound incense, and [set] the shewbread on the pure table; and [there is] the golden candlestick, and the lamps for burning, to light in the evening: for we keep the charge of the Lord God of our fathers; but ye have forsaken him.

pob.text: And behold[a], God is with us at our head, and his priests with the trumpets for the battle cry, to sound the alarm against you. Sons of Israel, do not fight against Yahweh, the God of your fathers, for you will not succeed.

spob.text: Look! God is with us, leading us from the front. His priests are also with us. They carry the trumpets for the battle cry, to sound the alarm against you. Sons of Israel,[a] do not fight against Yahweh, the God of your fathers, because you will not succeed.

public_domain_references.bsb: Now behold, God Himself is with us as our head, and His priests with their trumpets sound the battle call against you. O children of Israel, do not fight against the LORD, the God of your fathers, for you will not succeed.”
public_domain_references.web: Behold, God is with us at our head, and his priests with the trumpets of alarm to sound an alarm against you. Children of Israel, don’t fight against Yahweh, the God of your fathers; for you will not prosper.”

public_domain_references.kjv: And, behold, God himself [is] with us for [our] captain, and his priests with sounding trumpets to cry alarm against you. O children of Israel, fight ye not against the LORD God of your fathers; for ye shall not prosper.
public_domain_references.brenton: And, behold, the Lord and his priests are with us at our head, and the signal trumpets to sound an alarm over us. Children of Israel, fight not against the Lord God of our fathers; for ye shall not prosper.

pob.text: But Yarobam had turned the ambush around to come behind them, so they were in front of Judah, and the ambush was behind them.

spob.text: But Yarobam had sent an ambush around behind Judah. His forces were in front of Judah, while the ambush was behind them.

public_domain_references.bsb: Now Jeroboam had sent troops around to ambush from the rear, so that while he was in front of Judah, the ambush was behind them.

spob.text: When the people of Judah turned around, they saw that they were under attack from both the front and the rear. They cried out to Yahweh, and the priests were blowing the trumpets.

pob.text: Then the men of Judah raised a shout, and when the men of Judah shouted, God struck down Jeroboam and all Israel before Abijah and Judah.

spob.text: Judah’s men let out a shout. At the sound of their shout, God struck down Jeroboam and all Israel in front of Abijah and Judah.

pob.text: Abijah and his people struck them with a great blow[b][a], and five hundred thousand chosen men of Israel fell slain.

spob.text: Abijah and his people dealt them a severe blow, and 500,000 chosen men of Israel were killed.

public_domain_references.bsb: Then Abijah and his people struck them with a mighty blow, and 500,000 chosen men of Israel fell slain.
public_domain_references.web: Abijah and his people killed them with a great slaughter, so five hundred thousand chosen men of Israel fell down slain.

public_domain_references.brenton: And Abia and his people smote them with a great slaughter: and there fell slain of Israel five hundred thousand mighty men.

pob.text: So the sons of Israel were subdued at that time, and the sons of Judah prevailed, because they relied on Yahweh, the God of their fathers.

spob.text: So at that time the Israelites were subdued, and the people of Judah prevailed because they relied on Yahweh, the God of their fathers.

public_domain_references.kjv: Thus the children of Israel were brought under at that time, and the children of Judah prevailed, because they relied upon the LORD God of their fathers.
public_domain_references.brenton: So the children of Israel were brought low in that day, and the children of Juda prevailed, because they trusted on the Lord God of their fathers.

public_domain_references.brenton: And Jeroboam did not recover strength again all the days of Abia: and the Lord smote him, and he died.

pob.text: Asa did what was good and right in the eyes of Yahweh his God[a].

spob.text: Asa did what Yahweh his God considered good and right.

spob.text: He removed the high places used for worship and the incense altars[a] from every city in Judah. The kingdom was at peace under his rule.

spob.text: He built fortified cities in Judah. The land was quiet in those years, and he faced no war,[a] because Yahweh had given him rest.

public_domain_references.bsb: And now, here are the men of Ammon, Moab, and Mount Seir, whom You did not let Israel invade when they came out of the land of Egypt; but Israel turned away from them and did not destroy them.
public_domain_references.web: Now, behold, the children of Ammon and Moab and Mount Seir, whom you would not let Israel invade when they came out of the land of Egypt, but they turned away from them, and didn’t destroy them;
public_domain_references.asv: And now, behold, the children of Ammon and Moab and mount Seir, whom thou wouldest not let Israel invade, when they came out of the land of Egypt, but they turned aside from them, and destroyed them not;
public_domain_references.kjv: And now, behold, the children of Ammon and Moab and mount Seir, whom thou wouldest not let Israel invade, when they came out of the land of Egypt, but they turned from them, and destroyed them not;
public_domain_references.brenton: And now, behold, the children of Ammon, and Moab, and mount Seir, with regard to whom thou didst not permit Israel to pass through their border, when they had come out of the land of Egypt, (for they turned away from them, and did not destroy them;)—

pob.text: And behold[a], they are repaying us by coming to drive us out of your possession, which you gave us as an inheritance.

spob.text: See how they are repaying us! They are coming to drive us out of the land that belongs to you—the land you gave us as our inheritance.

public_domain_references.bsb: See how they are repaying us by coming to drive us out of the possession that You gave us as an inheritance.
public_domain_references.web: behold, how they reward us, to come to cast us out of your possession, which you have given us to inherit.
public_domain_references.asv: behold, how they reward us, to come to cast us out of thy possession, which thou hast given us to inherit.
public_domain_references.kjv: Behold, [I say, how] they reward us, to come to cast us out of thy possession, which thou hast given us to inherit.
public_domain_references.brenton: yet now, behold, they make attempts against us, to come forth to cast us out from our inheritance which thou gavest us.

pob.text: Our God[a], will you not judge them? For we have no power before this great multitude that is coming against us. We do not know what to do, but our eyes are on you.

spob.text: Our God, will you not judge them? We are powerless against this vast multitude coming against us. We do not know what to do, but our eyes are on you.

public_domain_references.bsb: Our God, will You not judge them? For we are powerless before this vast army that comes against us. We do not know what to do, but our eyes are upon You.”
public_domain_references.web: Our God, will you not judge them? For we have no might against this great company that comes against us. We don’t know what to do, but our eyes are on you.”
public_domain_references.asv: O our God, wilt thou not judge them? for we have no might against this great company that cometh against us; neither know we what to do: but our eyes are upon thee.
public_domain_references.kjv: O our God, wilt thou not judge them? for we have no might against this great company that cometh against us; neither know we what to do: but our eyes [are] upon thee.
public_domain_references.brenton: O Lord our God, wilt thou not judge them? for we have no strength to resist this great multitude that is come against us; and we know not what we shall do to them: but our eyes are toward thee.

pob.text: And all Judah was standing before Yahweh[a], even their little ones, their wives, and their children.

spob.text: All the people of Judah were standing before Yahweh, including their little ones, their wives, and their children.[a]

public_domain_references.bsb: Meanwhile all the men of Judah, with their wives and children and little ones, were standing before the LORD.
public_domain_references.web: All Judah stood before Yahweh, with their little ones, their wives, and their children.
public_domain_references.asv: And all Judah stood before Jehovah, with their little ones, their wives, and their children.
public_domain_references.kjv: And all Judah stood before the LORD, with their little ones, their wives, and their children.
public_domain_references.brenton: And all Juda was standing before the Lord, and their children, and their wives.

pob.text: And Jahaziel son of Zechariah, son of Benaiah, son of Jeiel, son of Mattaniah, the Levite, from the sons of Asaph—the Spirit of Yahweh came upon him in the midst of the assembly.

spob.text: Jahaziel was the son of Zechariah, son of Benaiah, son of Jeiel, son of Mattaniah. He was a Levite from among the descendants of Asaph. While he was among the gathered people, the Spirit of Yahweh came upon him.

public_domain_references.bsb: Then the Spirit of the LORD came upon Jahaziel son of Zechariah, the son of Benaiah, the son of Jeiel, the son of Mattaniah, a Levite from Asaph’s descendants, as he stood in the midst of the assembly.
public_domain_references.web: Then Yahweh’s Spirit came on Jahaziel the son of Zechariah, the son of Benaiah, the son of Jeiel, the son of Mattaniah, the Levite, of the sons of Asaph, in the middle of the assembly;
public_domain_references.asv: Then upon Jahaziel the son of Zechariah, the son of Benaiah, the son of Jeiel, the son of Mattaniah, the Levite, of the sons of Asaph, came the Spirit of Jehovah in the midst of the assembly;
public_domain_references.kjv: ¶ Then upon Jahaziel the son of Zechariah, the son of Benaiah, the son of Jeiel, the son of Mattaniah, a Levite of the sons of Asaph, came the Spirit of the LORD in the midst of the congregation;
public_domain_references.brenton: And Oziel the [son] of Zacharias, of the children of Banaias, of the sons of Eleïel the sons of Matthanias the Levite, of the sons of Asaph,—upon him came the Spirit of the Lord in the assembly:

pob.text: And he said[a], “Listen, all Judah and inhabitants of Jerusalem, and King Jehoshaphat: Thus says Yahweh to you, ‘Do not fear, and do not be dismayed because of this great multitude, for the battle is not yours, but God's.’”

spob.text: He said, “All you people of Judah, residents of Jerusalem, and King Jehoshaphat, listen! This is what Yahweh says to you: ‘Do not be afraid, and do not lose heart because of this vast army. The battle does not belong to you; it belongs to God.’”

public_domain_references.bsb: And he said, “Listen, all you people of Judah and Jerusalem! Listen, King Jehoshaphat! This is what the LORD says: ‘Do not be afraid or discouraged because of this vast army, for the battle does not belong to you, but to God.
public_domain_references.web: and he said, “Listen, all Judah, and you inhabitants of Jerusalem, and you, King Jehoshaphat. Yahweh says to you, ‘Don’t be afraid, and don’t be dismayed because of this great multitude; for the battle is not yours, but God’s.
public_domain_references.asv: and he said, Hearken ye, all Judah, and ye inhabitants of Jerusalem, and thou king Jehoshaphat: Thus saith Jehovah unto you, Fear not ye, neither be dismayed by reason of this great multitude; for the battle is not yours, but God’s.
public_domain_references.kjv: And he said, Hearken ye, all Judah, and ye inhabitants of Jerusalem, and thou king Jehoshaphat, Thus saith the LORD unto you, Be not afraid nor dismayed by reason of this great multitude; for the battle [is] not yours, but God’s.
public_domain_references.brenton: and he said, Hear ye, all Juda, and the dwellers in Jerusalem, and king Josaphat: Thus saith the Lord to you, even you, Fear not, neither be alarmed, before all this great multitude; for the battle is not yours, but God's.

pob.text: Tomorrow go down against them. Look[a], they are coming up by the ascent of Ziz, and you will find them at the end of the wadi, before the wilderness of Jeruel.

spob.text: Tomorrow, go down and confront them. Look! They are coming up the slope of Ziz. You will find them at the end of the ravine,[a] before the wilderness of Jeruel.

public_domain_references.bsb: Tomorrow you are to march down against them. You will see them coming up the Ascent of Ziz, and you will find them at the end of the valley facing the Wilderness of Jeruel.
public_domain_references.web: Tomorrow, go down against them. Behold, they are coming up by the ascent of Ziz. You will find them at the end of the valley, before the wilderness of Jeruel.
public_domain_references.asv: To-morrow go ye down against them: behold, they come up by the ascent of Ziz; and ye shall find them at the end of the valley, before the wilderness of Jeruel.
public_domain_references.kjv: To morrow go ye down against them: behold, they come up by the cliff of Ziz; and ye shall find them at the end of the brook, before the wilderness of Jeruel.
public_domain_references.brenton: To-morrow go ye down against them: behold, they come up by the ascent of Assis, and ye shall find them at the extremity of the river of the wilderness of Jeriel.

pob.text: You will not need to fight in this battle[a]. Take your positions, stand still, and see the salvation of Yahweh with you, O Judah and Jerusalem. Do not fear or be dismayed. Tomorrow go out before them[b], and Yahweh is with you.

spob.text: You will not have to fight this battle. Take your positions and stand firm. Watch Yahweh bring salvation to you,[a] people of Judah and Jerusalem. Do not be afraid or lose heart. Tomorrow, go out to face them. Yahweh is with you.[b]

public_domain_references.bsb: You need not fight this battle. Take up your positions, stand firm, and see the salvation of the LORD on your behalf, O Judah and Jerusalem. Do not be afraid or discouraged. Go out and face them tomorrow, for the LORD is with you.’”
public_domain_references.web: You will not need to fight this battle. Set yourselves, stand still, and see the salvation of Yahweh with you, O Judah and Jerusalem. Don’t be afraid, nor be dismayed. Go out against them tomorrow, for Yahweh is with you.’”
public_domain_references.asv: Ye shall not need to fight in this [battle]: set yourselves, stand ye still, and see the salvation of Jehovah with you, O Judah and Jerusalem; fear not, nor be dismayed: to-morrow go out against them; for Jehovah is with you.
public_domain_references.kjv: Ye shall not [need] to fight in this [battle:] set yourselves, stand ye [still], and see the salvation of the LORD with you, O Judah and Jerusalem: fear not, nor be dismayed; to morrow go out against them: for the LORD [will be] with you.
public_domain_references.brenton: It is not for you to fight: understand these things, and see the deliverance of the Lord with you, Juda and Jerusalem: fear not, neither be afraid to go forth to-morrow to meet them; and the Lord shall be with you.

pob.text: Then Jehoshaphat bowed with his face to the ground[a], and all Judah and the inhabitants of Jerusalem fell down before Yahweh to worship Yahweh.

spob.text: Then Jehoshaphat bowed with his face to the ground. All the people of Judah and those living in Jerusalem fell down before Yahweh to worship him.

public_domain_references.bsb: Then Jehoshaphat bowed facedown, and all the people of Judah and Jerusalem fell down before the LORD to worship Him.
public_domain_references.web: Jehoshaphat bowed his head with his face to the ground; and all Judah and the inhabitants of Jerusalem fell down before Yahweh, worshiping Yahweh.
public_domain_references.asv: And Jehoshaphat bowed his head with his face to the ground; and all Judah and the inhabitants of Jerusalem fell down before Jehovah, worshipping Jehovah.
public_domain_references.kjv: And Jehoshaphat bowed his head with [his] face to the ground: and all Judah and the inhabitants of Jerusalem fell before the LORD, worshipping the LORD.
public_domain_references.brenton: And Josaphat bowed with his face [to the ground] with all Juda and the dwellers in Jerusalem, [and] they fell before the Lord to worship the Lord.

pob.text: Then the Levites[a], from the sons of the Kohathites and from the sons of the Korahites, stood up to praise Yahweh, the God of Israel, with a very loud voice.

spob.text: Then Levites from the families descended from Kohath and from Korah stood up to praise Yahweh, the God of Israel, very loudly.

public_domain_references.bsb: And the Levites from the Kohathites and Korahites stood up to praise the LORD, the God of Israel, shouting in a very loud voice.
public_domain_references.web: The Levites, of the children of the Kohathites and of the children of the Korahites, stood up to praise Yahweh, the God of Israel, with an exceedingly loud voice.
public_domain_references.asv: And the Levites, of the children of the Kohathites and of the children of the Korahites, stood up to praise Jehovah, the God of Israel, with an exceeding loud voice.
public_domain_references.kjv: And the Levites, of the children of the Kohathites, and of the children of the Korhites, stood up to praise the LORD God of Israel with a loud voice on high.
public_domain_references.brenton: And the Levites of the children of Caath, and [they] of the sons of Core, rose up to praise the Lord God of Israel with a loud voice on high.

pob.text: They rose early in the morning and went out to the wilderness of Tekoa[a]. As they were going out, Jehoshaphat stood and said, “Listen to me, Judah and inhabitants of Jerusalem: believe in Yahweh your God, and you will be established; believe in his prophets[c][b], and you will succeed.”

spob.text: They got up early in the morning and went to the wilderness of Tekoa. As they were setting out, Jehoshaphat stood and said, “Listen to me, people of Judah and people of Jerusalem! Believe in Yahweh your God, and you will stand firm.[a] Believe in his prophets, and you will succeed.”

public_domain_references.bsb: Early in the morning they got up and left for the Wilderness of Tekoa. As they set out, Jehoshaphat stood up and said, “Hear me, O people of Judah and Jerusalem. Believe in the LORD your God, and you will be upheld; believe in His prophets, and you will succeed.”
public_domain_references.web: They rose early in the morning and went out into the wilderness of Tekoa. As they went out, Jehoshaphat stood and said, “Listen to me, Judah and you inhabitants of Jerusalem! Believe in Yahweh your God, so you will be established! Believe his prophets, so you will prosper.”
public_domain_references.asv: And they rose early in the morning, and went forth into the wilderness of Tekoa: and as they went forth, Jehoshaphat stood and said, Hear me, O Judah, and ye inhabitants of Jerusalem: believe in Jehovah your God, so shall ye be established; believe his prophets, so shall ye prosper.
public_domain_references.kjv: ¶ And they rose early in the morning, and went forth into the wilderness of Tekoa: and as they went forth, Jehoshaphat stood and said, Hear me, O Judah, and ye inhabitants of Jerusalem; Believe in the LORD your God, so shall ye be established; believe his prophets, so shall ye prosper.
public_domain_references.brenton: And they rose early in the morning and went out to the wilderness of Thecoe: and as they went out, Josaphat stood and cried, and said, Hear me, Juda, and the dwellers in Jerusalem; put your trust in the Lord God, and your trust shall be honoured; trust in his prophet, and ye shall prosper.

pob.text: After consulting with the people[a], he appointed singers to Yahweh, who praised the splendor of holiness as they went out before the vanguard, saying, “Give thanks to Yahweh[c][b], for his steadfast love endures forever.”

spob.text: After consulting with the people, he appointed singers to sing to Yahweh and praise the beauty of holiness.[a] They went out ahead of the advance troops and said, “Give thanks to Yahweh, for his steadfast love[b] endures forever.”

public_domain_references.bsb: Then Jehoshaphat consulted with the people and appointed those who would sing to the LORD and praise the splendor of His holiness. As they went out before the army, they were singing: “Give thanks to the LORD, for His loving devotion endures forever.”
public_domain_references.web: When he had taken counsel with the people, he appointed those who were to sing to Yahweh and give praise in holy array as they go out before the army, and say, “Give thanks to Yahweh, for his loving kindness endures forever.”
public_domain_references.asv: And when he had taken counsel with the people, he appointed them that should sing unto Jehovah, and give praise in holy array, as they went out before the army, and say, Give thanks unto Jehovah; for his lovingkindness [endureth] for ever.
public_domain_references.kjv: And when he had consulted with the people, he appointed singers unto the LORD, and that should praise the beauty of holiness, as they went out before the army, and to say, Praise the LORD; for his mercy [endureth] for ever.
public_domain_references.brenton: And he took counsel with the people, and set appointed men to sing psalms and praises, to give thanks, and sing the holy songs of praise in going forth before the host: and they said, Give thanks to the Lord, for his mercy [endures] for ever.

pob.text: And at the time they began with singing and praise[a], Yahweh set ambushes against the Ammonites, Moab, and Mount Seir, who were coming against Judah[b], and they were struck down.

spob.text: When they began to sing and praise, Yahweh set ambushes[a] against the Ammonites, the Moabites, and the people from Mount Seir, who were coming to attack Judah. The invaders were struck down.

public_domain_references.bsb: The moment they began their shouts and praises, the LORD set ambushes against the men of Ammon, Moab, and Mount Seir who had come against Judah, and they were defeated.
public_domain_references.web: When they began to sing and to praise, Yahweh set ambushers against the children of Ammon, Moab, and Mount Seir, who had come against Judah; and they were struck.
public_domain_references.asv: And when they began to sing and to praise, Jehovah set liers-in-wait against the children of Ammon, Moab, and mount Seir, that were come against Judah; and they were smitten.
public_domain_references.kjv: ¶ And when they began to sing and to praise, the LORD set ambushments against the children of Ammon, Moab, and mount Seir, which were come against Judah; and they were smitten.
public_domain_references.brenton: And when they began the praise and thanksgiving, the Lord caused the children of Ammon to fight against Moab, and [the inhabitants of] mount Seir that came out against Juda; and they were routed.

pob.text: Then the Ammonites and Moabites rose up against the inhabitants of Mount Seir to devote them to destruction and to wipe them out; and when they had finished with the inhabitants of Seir[a], they helped each other to destroy one another.

spob.text: Then the Ammonites and Moabites attacked the people of Mount Seir. They devoted them to destruction[a] and wiped them out. When they had finished destroying the people of Seir, they helped destroy one another.

public_domain_references.bsb: The Ammonites and Moabites rose up against the inhabitants of Mount Seir, devoting them to destruction. And when they had made an end to the inhabitants of Seir, they helped to destroy one another.
public_domain_references.web: For the children of Ammon and Moab stood up against the inhabitants of Mount Seir to utterly kill and destroy them. When they had finished the inhabitants of Seir, everyone helped to destroy each other.
public_domain_references.asv: For the children of Ammon and Moab stood up against the inhabitants of mount Seir, utterly to slay and destroy them: and when they had made an end of the inhabitants of Seir, every one helped to destroy another.
public_domain_references.kjv: For the children of Ammon and Moab stood up against the inhabitants of mount Seir, utterly to slay and destroy [them:] and when they had made an end of the inhabitants of Seir, every one helped to destroy another.
public_domain_references.brenton: Then the children of Ammon and Moab rose up against the dwellers in mount Seir, to destroy and consume them; and when they had made an end of [destroying] the inhabitants of Seir, they rose up against one another so that they were utterly destroyed.

pob.text: When Judah came to the lookout over the wilderness[a], they turned toward the multitude, and behold, there were corpses lying on the ground, and there was no survivor.

spob.text: When the people of Judah reached the lookout over the wilderness, they turned toward the enemy forces. There before them were corpses lying on the ground. Not one person had survived.

public_domain_references.bsb: When the men of Judah came to a place overlooking the wilderness, they looked for the vast army, but there were only corpses lying on the ground; no one had escaped.
public_domain_references.web: When Judah came to the place overlooking the wilderness, they looked at the multitude; and behold, they were dead bodies fallen to the earth, and there were none who escaped.
public_domain_references.asv: And when Judah came to the watch-tower of the wilderness, they looked upon the multitude; and, behold, they were dead bodies fallen to the earth, and there were none that escaped.
public_domain_references.kjv: And when Judah came toward the watch tower in the wilderness, they looked unto the multitude, and, behold, they [were] dead bodies fallen to the earth, and none escaped.
public_domain_references.brenton: And Juda came to the watch-tower of the wilderness, and looked, and saw the multitude, and, behold, [they were] all fallen dead upon the earth, not one escaped.

pob.text: Then Jehoshaphat and his people came to plunder their spoil[a], and they found among them in abundance goods, garments, and desirable articles; and they took for themselves more than they could carry. They were three days plundering the spoil, because it was so much.

spob.text: Then Jehoshaphat and his people went to take the plunder. Among the fallen enemy forces they found a great amount of goods, corpses[a], and valuable objects. They took more than they could carry away. They spent three days taking the plunder because there was so much of it.

public_domain_references.bsb: Then Jehoshaphat and his people went to carry off the plunder, and they found on the bodies an abundance of goods and valuables —more than they could carry away. They were gathering the plunder for three days because there was so much.
public_domain_references.web: When Jehoshaphat and his people came to take their plunder, they found among them in abundance both riches and dead bodies with precious jewels, which they stripped off for themselves, more than they could carry away. They took plunder for three days, it was so much.
public_domain_references.asv: And when Jehoshaphat and his people came to take the spoil of them, they found among them in abundance both riches and dead bodies, and precious jewels, which they stripped off for themselves, more than they could carry away: and they were three days in taking the spoil, it was so much.
public_domain_references.kjv: And when Jehoshaphat and his people came to take away the spoil of them, they found among them in abundance both riches with the dead bodies, and precious jewels, which they stripped off for themselves, more than they could carry away: and they were three days in gathering of the spoil, it was so much.
public_domain_references.brenton: And Josaphat and his people went out to spoil them, and they found much cattle, and furniture, and spoils, and precious things: and they spoiled them, and they were three days gathering the spoil, for it was abundant.

pob.text: On the fourth day they assembled in the Valley of Beracah[a], because there they blessed Yahweh. Therefore they called the name of that place the Valley of Beracah to this day.

spob.text: On the fourth day, they gathered in the Valley of Beracah.[a] They blessed Yahweh there, so they named the place the Valley of Beracah. It is still called that today.

public_domain_references.bsb: On the fourth day they assembled in the Valley of Beracah, where they blessed the LORD. Therefore that place is called the Valley of Beracah to this day.
public_domain_references.web: On the fourth day, they assembled themselves in Beracah Valley, for there they blessed Yahweh. Therefore the name of that place was called “Beracah Valley” to this day.
public_domain_references.asv: And on the fourth day they assembled themselves in the valley of Beracah; for there they blessed Jehovah: therefore the name of that place was called The valley of Beracah unto this day.
public_domain_references.kjv: ¶ And on the fourth day they assembled themselves in the valley of Berachah; for there they blessed the LORD: therefore the name of the same place was called, The valley of Berachah, unto this day.
public_domain_references.brenton: And it came to pass on the fourth day they were gathered to the Valley of Blessing; for there they blessed the Lord: therefore they called the name of that place the Valley of Blessing, until this day.

pob.text: Then all the men of Judah and Jerusalem returned[a], with Jehoshaphat at their head, to return to Jerusalem with joy[b], because Yahweh had made them rejoice over their enemies.

spob.text: Then all the men of Judah and Jerusalem returned joyfully to Jerusalem, with Jehoshaphat leading them, because Yahweh had made them rejoice over their enemies.

public_domain_references.bsb: Then all the men of Judah and Jerusalem, with Jehoshaphat at their head, returned joyfully to Jerusalem, for the LORD had made them rejoice over their enemies.
public_domain_references.web: Then they returned, every man of Judah and Jerusalem, with Jehoshaphat in front of them, to go again to Jerusalem with joy; for Yahweh had made them to rejoice over their enemies.
public_domain_references.asv: Then they returned, every man of Judah and Jerusalem, and Jehoshaphat in the forefront of them, to go again to Jerusalem with joy; for Jehovah had made them to rejoice over their enemies.
public_domain_references.kjv: Then they returned, every man of Judah and Jerusalem, and Jehoshaphat in the forefront of them, to go again to Jerusalem with joy; for the LORD had made them to rejoice over their enemies.
public_domain_references.brenton: And all the men of Juda returned to Jerusalem, and Josaphat led them with great joy; for the Lord gave them joy over their enemies.

pob.text: And they came to Jerusalem with harps and lyres and trumpets[b][a], to the house of Yahweh.

spob.text: They came to Yahweh’s house in Jerusalem with harps[a], lyres, and trumpets.[b]

public_domain_references.bsb: So they entered Jerusalem and went into the house of the LORD with harps, lyres, and trumpets.
public_domain_references.web: They came to Jerusalem with stringed instruments, harps, and trumpets to Yahweh’s house.
public_domain_references.asv: And they came to Jerusalem with psalteries and harps and trumpets unto the house of Jehovah.
public_domain_references.kjv: And they came to Jerusalem with psalteries and harps and trumpets unto the house of the LORD.
public_domain_references.brenton: And they entered into Jerusalem with lutes and harps and trumpets, [going] into the house of the Lord.

pob.text: And the fear of God came upon all the kingdoms of the lands when they heard that Yahweh had fought against the enemies of Israel[a].

spob.text: Dread of God came over all the kingdoms of the lands when they heard that Yahweh had fought against Israel’s enemies.[a]

public_domain_references.bsb: And the fear of God came upon all the kingdoms of the lands when they heard that the LORD had fought against the enemies of Israel.
public_domain_references.web: The fear of God was on all the kingdoms of the countries when they heard that Yahweh fought against the enemies of Israel.
public_domain_references.asv: And the fear of God was on all the kingdoms of the countries, when they heard that Jehovah fought against the enemies of Israel.
public_domain_references.kjv: And the fear of God was on all the kingdoms of [those] countries, when they had heard that the LORD fought against the enemies of Israel.
public_domain_references.brenton: And there was a terror of the Lord upon all the kingdoms of the land, when they heard that the Lord fought against the enemies of Israel.

pob.text: So the kingdom of Jehoshaphat was at peace[a], and his God gave him rest all around.

spob.text: So Jehoshaphat’s kingdom was at peace, and his God gave him rest from threats on every side.

public_domain_references.bsb: Then Jehoshaphat’s kingdom was at peace, for his God had given him rest on every side.
public_domain_references.web: So the realm of Jehoshaphat was quiet, for his God gave him rest all around.
public_domain_references.asv: So the realm of Jehoshaphat was quiet; for his God gave him rest round about.
public_domain_references.kjv: So the realm of Jehoshaphat was quiet: for his God gave him rest round about.
public_domain_references.brenton: And the kingdom of Josaphat was at peace; and his God gave him rest round about.

pob.text: And Jehoshaphat reigned over Judah. He was thirty-five years old when he began to reign, and he reigned twenty-five years in Jerusalem. And his mother’s name was Azubah daughter of Shilhi.

spob.text: Jehoshaphat became king of Judah at age thirty-five. He ruled in Jerusalem for twenty-five years. His mother was Azubah, the daughter of Shilhi.

public_domain_references.bsb: So Jehoshaphat reigned over Judah. He was thirty-five years old when he became king, and he reigned in Jerusalem twenty-five years. His mother’s name was Azubah daughter of Shilhi.

pob.text: However[a], the high places were not removed, and the people still had not set their hearts toward the God of their fathers.

spob.text: However, the worship sites known as high places were not removed. The people still had not set their hearts on the God of their ancestors.

public_domain_references.brenton: Nevertheless the high places yet remained; and as yet the people did not direct their heart to the Lord God of their fathers.

pob.text: The rest of the acts of Jehoshaphat[a], the first and the last, behold, they are written in the records of Jehu son of Hanani[b], which are included in the Book of the Kings of Israel.

spob.text: All the other things Jehoshaphat did, from beginning to end, are recorded in the writings of Jehu son of Hanani. These writings are included in the Book of the Kings of Israel.[a]

spob.text: Later, King Jehoshaphat of Judah formed an alliance with King Ahaziah of Israel. Ahaziah acted wickedly in what he did.[a]

pob.text: So he allied himself with him to make ships to go to Tarshish[b][a], and they made ships at Ezion-geber.

spob.text: So Jehoshaphat joined Ahaziah in a partnership to build ships bound for Tarshish. They built the ships at Ezion-geber.

public_domain_references.brenton: by acting [with] and going to him, to build ships to go to Tharsis: and he built ships in Gasion Gaber.

pob.text: And Jehoshaphat slept with his fathers and was buried with his fathers in the city of David[b][a], and Jehoram his son reigned in his place.

pob.text: And he had brothers[a], the sons of Jehoshaphat: Azariah, Jehiel, Zechariah, Azariahu, Michael, and Shephatiah[b]. All these were the sons of Jehoshaphat king of Israel.

pob.text: When Jehoram had risen over his father's kingdom and had strengthened himself[a], he killed all his brothers with the sword, and also some of the princes of Israel.

pob.text: Jehoram was thirty-two years old when he became king, and he reigned eight years in Jerusalem.

pob.text: Yet Yahweh was not willing to destroy the house of David[a], because of the covenant that he had made with David[c][b], and as he had said that he would give to him and to his sons a lamp for all days.

spob.text: Yet Yahweh was not willing to destroy the house of David—David’s royal family line—because of the covenant he had made with David, just as he had said that he would give David and his sons a lamp for all days—a picture of their continuing royal line.[a]

pob.text: He also made high places in the hill country of Judah[a], led the inhabitants of Jerusalem into prostitution[b], and led Judah astray.

pob.text: They came up against Judah and invaded it[a], and carried away all the possessions found in the king’s house, and also his sons and his wives, so that no son was left to him except Jehoahaz, the youngest of his sons.

spob.text: They marched against Judah and broke into the land. They carried away all the property they found in the king’s palace, along with his sons and wives. No son was left to him except Jehoahaz,[a] his youngest son.

public_domain_references.bsb: So they went to war against Judah, invaded it, and carried off all the possessions found in the king’s palace, along with his sons and wives; not a son was left to him except Jehoahaz, his youngest.
public_domain_references.web: and they came up against Judah, broke into it, and carried away all the possessions that were found in the king’s house, including his sons and his wives, so that there was no son left to him except Jehoahaz, the youngest of his sons.
public_domain_references.asv: and they came up against Judah, and brake into it, and carried away all the substance that was found in the king’s house, and his sons also, and his wives; so that there was never a son left him, save Jehoahaz, the youngest of his sons.
public_domain_references.kjv: And they came up into Judah, and brake into it, and carried away all the substance that was found in the king’s house, and his sons also, and his wives; so that there was never a son left him, save Jehoahaz, the youngest of his sons.
